title: How CBT Has Proven Its Effectiveness
description: This article looks at the scientific evidence for the effectiveness of cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) in treating depression, anxiety disorders, PTSD, and panic attacks. It also emphasizes the importance of working with professionals and explains when CBT alone may not be enough.

texts: CBT’s journey to recognition was far from easy, and certainly not rapid.

In its early stages, Beck’s theory was criticized by Freudians and other colleagues—it was labeled “superficial,” and its effectiveness was questioned due to a lack of sufficient scientific grounding. Even pharmaceutical companies opposed it, seeing successful therapy as competition for psychotropic drugs.
It took time, research, and substantial data for CBT to establish its evidence-based foundation.
1977 was a turning point: Beck’s research showed that CBT helped patients with depression more effectively than imipramine—one of the most powerful antidepressants of that time.
Many years have passed since then, and today there are more than 200 major studies confirming the effectiveness of CBT in a wide variety of situations.
Here are just a few examples showing that CBT works for various psychological challenges:

• Depression: A study by Tad Jude and colleagues (2012) showed that after 14–16 sessions, improvement was observed in 40–60% of patients. Furthermore, the therapy reduced the risk of relapse by 50–60% in the long term.
• Anxiety disorders: Data from Norton and colleagues (2018) showed effectiveness in 46–66% of cases for generalized anxiety, with long-lasting effects.
• PTSD: A study by Schneider and colleagues (2014) showed significant improvement in 60–72% of patients with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD); the effect was also long-lasting.
• Panic attacks: A study by Barlow and colleagues (2017) showed a reduction in the frequency and intensity of panic attacks in 60–75% of patients. The improvements were stable.
<q author="Johann Wolfgang von Goethe">They say that numbers rule the world. No, they only show how the world is ruled.</q>

test.question: Which of the following statements about CBT is incorrect?
answers: It has proven its effectiveness in numerous scientific experiments
It is suitable for people with depression, anxiety, and panic attacks
It treats severe mental disorders better than medication
It faced skepticism in its early stages

texts: We have discussed where CBT is truly effective. Now, it is important to note where its capabilities may fall short.
For severe mental disorders, such as schizophrenia or bipolar disorder, CBT alone is usually not enough—medication and medical supervision are typically required.
Avoid self-diagnosing—only a specialist can objectively assess your condition.
Always consult a professional. Your mental well-being is a vital part of your life, and it deserves attentive and caring treatment.
